feed.title: Type-Safe Computer Vision
feed.subtitle: Computer vision bugs that are type bugs, and how a type system makes them unrepresentable.

entry.title: The Blue Face Bug
entry.summary: Three bytes in memory do not say which channel comes first. Read as RGB they are a warm skin tone; read as BGR they are ice-blue. A blue face on screen is a funny bug; a blue face inside a tensor is a silent one. Why RGB/BGR confusion is a type bug, and what it looks like when the compiler catches it.

entry.title: 128 Is Not the Middle
entry.summary: Average a black pixel and a white pixel. You wrote (0 + 255) / 2 and got 128, but 128 carries only about 22% of the light, so the answer is visibly wrong. The correct value is 188. Gamma-encoded pixels break every naive resize, blur, and blend, and the fix belongs in the type system.
